summary:
Attempt 2 fixes both findings as the decisions asked.
- **R2-m2:** IsMisparsed now tests the whole component. `C:\con.txt` moved into the addressable theory.
- **Resolve-back check (new):** Walk refuses any S_OK parse whose ID list does not resolve back to the target (ParsedAsAnotherItem). Its SamePath / LongName logic holds past MAX_PATH:
  - With 8.3 names, the shell hands back an 8.3 path. On C: I measured 300 and 1000 characters, plus deep paths of 10-char and 8-char components where even the 8.3 form exceeds 260.
  - On D:, which has no 8.3 names, the shell hands back a `\\?\` path at 304 and 1004 characters. It is still resolved and matched, because LongPath.ToExtended passes `\\?\` through. So the new check does not undo the landings the spike measured on D:.
- **m1:** Compare-ExplorerState is now a multiset over Hwnd|Folder|Selected. Close-CaseWindows no longer uses a baseline and quits an entry only when every entry with its HWND is under the case roots.
- **Return-shape fix:** Watch-ExplorerUnchanged's unary-comma return is fixed. My first round missed it, and it would have failed R-001 step 3 every time.

What I ran, all green:
- Full suite: 503/503.
- App build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- Fitness (rebuilt): 69 rules hold.
- WindowCases.ps1: parses with 0 errors.

**Two new findings.** Both are minor, and both are in window-test code this review has already passed once:
- **m3:** R-002 calls `[void](Check-Landing ...)`, which throws away every Check line inside it, FAIL lines and the 'landed N ms after the click' figure included. The runner prints only 'FAILED: R-002' or 'PASSED'. I showed this by loading the real functions from the script and feeding them a landing of 1400 ms: it was recorded as a failure, and 0 lines were printed.
- **m4:** Close-CaseWindows judges whether a window holds anything of the person's from Get-ExplorerWindows. That function drops any entry whose Document is null or whose read throws. So such a tab of the person's cannot stop the case from calling Quit() on its own tab in the same window. That Quit() is the call whose reach (one tab or the whole window) was never measured.

**Still not run:** steps a–d of R-002 and all of R-001 have not been run by any stage.

Second round: This round found nothing new. The two minor findings from this attempt's first round still stand and are not withdrawn:
- **m3:** `[void](Check-Landing ...)` swallows the landing checks and the timing lines.
- **m4:** Close-CaseWindows judges a window by Get-ExplorerWindows, which drops unreadable entries.

What this round checked, adversarially, across attempt 2's changes:
- **Resolve-back check, measured with parse-only probes (no window opened), using the same logic as SamePath and LongName:**
  - Past MAX_PATH on C:, where the shell hands back 8.3 paths.
  - Deep 8-character and 10-character components on C:, whose 8.3 form exceeds 260, where it hands back `\\?\` paths.
  - At 300 and 1000 characters on D:, which has no 8.3 names, again `\\?\` paths.
  - Unusual names: emoji, NFD combining accent, `#&=`, a literal `x~1.txt`, an RTL override, semicolons, a dotted folder and a file inside it, a `folder.{CLSID}` name, and an upper-case extension.
  - Every one parsed S_OK and was judged the same item, so the check falsely refuses none of these shapes.
- **Other boundaries and error paths:**
  - SamePath on roots and UNC paths, and on an empty or null path coming back.
  - PathOfIdList's buffer and its `[Out] char[]` marshalling.
  - IsMisparsed after the change: its trailing-space trim is now a no-op, and `COM¹` / `CONIN$` are still refused.
  - The real-tree test's dependence on how long %TEMP% is: a path over 300 characters holds for any TEMP longer than about 5 characters.
  - Compare-ExplorerState's multiset keys and HWND formatting.
  - Close-CaseWindows' return shape.
  - Every output-capturing call site in R-001 and R-002. Only the four `[void](Check-Landing ...)` sites already filed as m3 swallow Check output; Invoke-WatchedReveal and Invoke-RefusedReveal emit nothing but their result object.

Tests, build, rules-parity and Fitness were green in this attempt's first round.

findings.claim: R-002 calls every landing check as `[void](Check-Landing ...)`. Check and CheckEqual report through Write-Output, and the run section prints only 'FAILED: <keys>' or 'PASSED', never the contents of $script:Failures. So every line Check-Landing produces is thrown away: the ok and FAIL lines for the exit code, the logged path, the kind, whether the hook saw the command start, whether the step landed, 'landed after the click', 'within 1000 ms', and the 'landed N ms after the click' figure. A step that misses the 1 s bound or never lands still fails the case, so there is no false pass. But the output says only 'FAILED: R-002', with no step, check or millisecond figure. A passing run records no landing time for criterion 2. Validate runs this case unattended to settle criteria 1, 2 and 5 and the cold-reveal bound, so both outcomes come back without their evidence.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:4131, 4138, 4148 and 4164, `[void](Check-Landing ...)`. Check at :146-154 uses Write-Output. The run section at the end of the file prints only FAILED or PASSED. I loaded Show, Check, CheckEqual and Check-Landing from the script's AST and fed them a reveal that landed 1400 ms after the click. Called as R-002 calls it, 0 lines were printed and 1 failure was recorded ('...landed within 1000 ms of the click (1400 ms)'). Called without [void], 10 lines were printed, including '  FAIL  the 300-character file landed within 1000 ms of the click (1400 ms)'.
findings.fix: Drop the `return $ms` / `return -1` values from Check-Landing, since no caller uses them. Then call it plainly (`Check-Landing $r $file ... $true`) at the four call sites, so its Check lines and the timing line reach the runner's output like every other step's checks.

findings.claim: Close-CaseWindows decides whether a window holds anything of the person's by looking only at Get-ExplorerWindows' output. That function silently drops any Shell.Application entry whose Document is null or whose read throws (for example a tab mid-navigation, or one rejecting the COM call while busy). So when a case tab shares its HWND with one of the person's tabs that is unreadable at that moment, `$others` comes out empty and the case calls Quit() on its own tab. Whether Quit() on one tab's entry closes only that tab or the whole window was never measured, which is why the decision required this path never to Quit a window that might hold the person's tabs. The safe branch the build chose is therefore only as safe as the read that fed it, and at worst it closes the person's Explorer window. Reaching it takes two things at once: Explorer puts a case reveal into the person's window as a tab, and one of the person's tabs is unreadable during the poll.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:3429 `if ($null -eq $doc) { continue }` and :3436 `catch { }` in Get-ExplorerWindows. In Close-CaseWindows, :3499 `$others = @($windows | Where-Object { $_.Hwnd -eq $w.Hwnd -and -not (Test-Under $_.Folder $roots) })` is computed over those filtered $windows, and :3501 calls `$w.Window.Quit()`. The decision on m1 said: 'confirm that Quit() on one tab's Shell.Application entry closes only that tab ... If it closes the whole window, close the tab another way, or fail the isolation check with the folder named, and do not Quit it.'
findings.fix: In Close-CaseWindows, count the raw entries per HWND straight from `(New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).Windows()`, reading only `.HWND` inside its own try. An entry whose HWND cannot be read counts as the person's. Quit a case entry only when that raw count for its HWND equals the number of case entries with that HWND; otherwise report it by folder, as for a mixed window now.

obligations.evidence: R-002 step (a) in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 feeds a FullControl deny that is verified unlistable before the scan. The Core side is exercised by the real-tree unit test, where the deny-all folder reaches the open. No stage has run the window step.
R-002 step (b): exactly 161 characters, timed. Never run. If it had been, its checks would not have been printed (m3).
R-002 step (b): 300 characters from its largest: row, plus R-001 step 10 padded to exactly 300. Neither has run.
R-002 step (d): 1000 characters from its largest: row. Never run. The Core resolve-back holds at this length on C: (8.3 path back) and on D: (\\?\ path back), per my parse-only probe.
R-002 step (c): a 300-character deny-all folder from its tree: row. Never run.
The step order b,a,c,d,e makes the 161-character reveal the first one in a -Case R-002 run. Never run.
R-002 step (d) pre-opens the parent with the sibling selected, then needs exactly one selected item. Never run.
ShellRevealTests.Walk_OnRealTree_RefusesGoneTargetsAndLandsThePresentOne passes in my run (503/503). The builder recorded R-002 step (e) passing again with the string-keyed compare.
The real-tree test's kept\deleted.bin, plus the Walk_TargetNoLongerExists theory. Both pass.
Walk_OpenFails_RefusesWithItsCodeFreesTheIdListAndTriesNothingElse passes. Its default FakeShell pathOf returns the parsed path, so the open is still reached.
SelectSwitchRuleTests passes. rules-parity reports AGREE, and Fitness reports 69 rules holding.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Compare-ExplorerState keys each entry as "$Hwnd|$Folder|$Selected" in a List and removes matches as a multiset, so two tabs sharing an HWND no longer read as a move. Close-CaseWindows (:3493) has no baseline and quits an entry only when no same-HWND entry lies outside the roots, which is the decision's safe branch. Isolation checks name the folders left. The baselineHwnds plumbing is gone from R-001 and R-002. One remaining gap in that safe branch is filed as m4.

src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs IsMisparsed now uses `baseName = component.TrimEnd(' ')`. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ShellRevealTests.cs moved C:\con.txt, and added aux.h, nul.log, com1.txt, prn.md and con.d\inner.bin, into Plan_UnusualAddressableNames_StaysExact. The real-tree test sends con.txt, aux.h, nul.log, com1.txt and con.d\inner.bin through the real shell as Exact, and all pass. There is no Windows 10 branch, as the decision said; the resolve-back check is the backstop.

drift: Two statements are now stale. ShellReveal.cs:206 (Walk's doc: 'Exact comes from the shell's S_OK alone') and docs/design/SL-088-reveal-lands-or-refuses.md:45 ('`Exact` still comes from the shell's S_OK alone') both predate attempt 2. Exact now also requires the parsed ID list to resolve back to the target (ParsedAsAnotherItem). Both lines are still right that Explorer's window is never consulted, but the 'alone' is no longer true.

MainWindow.xaml.cs RevealFailure's comment ('Windows' message for a FACILITY_WIN32 HRESULT, and the HRESULT itself for any other') describes only two of its four branches. It leaves out NameUnaddressable and the new ParsedAsAnotherItem. The ParsedAsAnotherItem text, 'Explorer reads its path as another item', is also shown when SHGetPathFromIDListEx returns no path at all.

Declared, but worth the next reader's attention: the resolve-back check adds a GetLongPathNameW import in Core (ShellReveal.cs) that sits outside Kernel32.CriticalErrorBoxOff. SL-077's guarded-open rule does not list that function. It is reached only after the shell has parsed the path S_OK and the text differs, so a no-media drive would already have failed the parse before it.

Measured here in a parse-only probe (no window), beyond the build's own measurements: on D:, an NTFS volume with no 8.3 names, and on C: with deep paths whose 8.3 form exceeds 260, SHGetPathFromIDListEx returns a \\?\-prefixed path. SamePath still matches it through LongPath.ToExtended/ToDisplay. No unit test feeds the \\?\ path-back shape; the real-tree test covers only the 8.3 one.

Nothing new beyond this attempt's first round. The stale 'Exact comes from the shell's S_OK alone' lines at ShellReveal.cs:206 and in the design note, and the incomplete RevealFailure comment, still stand as recorded there.
